clue.text: Golden boy, unlined, in bloom

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: un-L-ined: the word for the boy loses its L, read as 'un-L'

parts.note: a boy is a child
the letter L named by 'unlined'

explanation.surface: A golden boy, without wrinkles, is in the bloom of youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlined' is read as 'L removed', taking L from CHILD to leave CHID.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flower, so it is one kind of bloom.

clue.text: Old king, see, away from capital sometimes

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia

indicators.note: away from says the second word is taken out of the first

parts.note: London is the capital of England
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: An old king, seeing his see, stays away from the capital some of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes LO from LONDON, leaving NDON. 'see' looks like a bishop's diocese but means 'look!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something intermittently means at some times and not others.

clue.text: More attractive republican slogan?

definitions.meaning: a republican might chant '...', ER being the monarch

explanation.surface: A political catchphrase claiming something is more appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuter is the comparative of cute, meaning more appealing or sweeter.

clue.text: Nigerian witchcraft taken up

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: obi (obeah) is a West Indian form of witchcraft

explanation.surface: A Nigerian takes up witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ibo, or Igbo, are a people of south-eastern Nigeria.

clue.text: Put one's foot in it, being married, losing a ring during the event

indicators.note: losing says a piece is dropped from the word for the event

parts.note: an occasion is an event
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone commits a gaffe at a wedding by losing the ring during the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes one O out of OCCASION to leave OCCASIN; 'during' is a link. The definition is playful: a moccasin is something you literally put your foot in.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft shoe, which is what one literally puts a foot into.

clue.text: Model train fitted to popular gauge in part of N America

indicators.note: fitted to puts the rearranged letters inside the gauge

parts.note: OO gauge is the most popular model railway scale in Britain

indicators.note: model as a verb means shape anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A model train is set up on a popular track gauge, somewhere in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gauge' looks like a measuring verb, but in model railways O and OO are track scales; 'Model' signals the anagram and 'fitted to' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a province of Canada, so it is a region of North America.

clue.text: Almost heal illness — after time, premature end

indicators.note: after says the illness word follows the time letter
almost means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: to cure is to heal
the final letter dropped by 'Almost'
an ailment is an illness

explanation.surface: Treatment of an illness is cut short too early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter, and 'after' puts the time letter before the illness; the dash is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtailment is a cutting short, an end that comes before it should.

clue.text: Facing this, carp not landed in dinghy

indicators.note: in puts the landowning word inside the boat

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
acred means owning land

explanation.surface: An angler in a dinghy fails to land a carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like the fish but means to complain: a sacred cow is something you must not criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea held beyond criticism, so in its presence you must not complain.

clue.text: Roman fails Latin at first — is that expected?

indicators.note: fails suggests the word breaks down, so its letters are rearranged
at first takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A Roman student fails Latin — is that what you would expect?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' rearranges ROMAN into NORMA, then L comes from 'Latin at first'; 'is that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal is usual and so what one would anticipate.

clue.text: One can count up millions in ancient civilisation

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the civilisation's name

parts.note: Sumer was an ancient civilisation in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone can tally the millions in an ancient civilisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads the answer as 'one who sums', not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer, literally, is a person who adds numbers, one who totals figures.

clue.text: What good bra should do, with extra energy

definitions.meaning: a well-made bra is shaped to suit the wearer's bust
an idiom meaning with great vigour, as in laughing or straining fit to burst

explanation.surface: A lingerie tip about a good bra, plus some advice to put your back into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is usually 'fit to burst'; the clue plays on the near-identical sound, so bra fit and bursting energy share one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A properly sized bra is literally fitted to the bust, and the phrase also suggests bursting with vigour.

clue.text: School lesson given by scoundrel: come again?

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A rogue teaches a school lesson, and someone asks him to repeat himself.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a lesson in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again, so it means to come back once more.

clue.text: County of birth our man cunningly concealed

indicators.note: cunningly disguised letters are reshuffled so the place name is not obvious

explanation.surface: A man's birthplace county is being slyly kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly concealed' tells you to rearrange BIRTH OUR MAN; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Northumbria names the historic north-eastern region, roughly the modern county of Northumberland in England.

clue.text: Keble College's first to move in race for Finn

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for race

parts.note: to race is to hurry

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of College's
to move tells you the letters change places

explanation.surface: Keble College's best rower is moved into a race for Finland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion; 'for' is a link. Keble is an Oxford college, and 'Finn' is Mark Twain's surname for the character.
explanation.definitionFit: Huck Finn, Mark Twain's character, has the given name Huckleberry.

clue.text: Worried about getting letter

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: if something worried you, it ate at you ('what's eating you?')

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about receiving a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ATE round; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Policeman is away to the cooler

parts.note: off means away, as in 'off on holiday'
an icer is something that chills

explanation.surface: A constable heads off to put someone in the cooler, slang for prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cooler' looks like slang for a jail cell, but it means something that cools. 'is' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is a policeman, the rank-and-file term in many forces.

clue.text: Maybe cover sore, initially inflamed horribly

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order
initially takes the opening letter of sore

explanation.surface: A medical note: perhaps cover the sore, which is badly inflamed at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a fielding position in cricket; 'horribly' rearranges S plus INFLAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a player stationed at cover point is a fielder, so cover is an example.

clue.text: It's exactly the hour, commander, to shut up

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
to lock is to shut securely

explanation.surface: A commander announces the time and orders silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' looks like an order to be quiet, but it means to secure with a key.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is said after a number to mark the time exactly on the hour, as in 'six on the dot'.

clue.text: Brown, with another colour: black skin was preeminent

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
rind is the tough skin of fruit or cheese
led means was in front

explanation.surface: A black-skinned animal, brown with another hue, was the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindled describes a brownish coat streaked with another colour, as on some dogs.

clue.text: State of luxury was common under Cromwell

indicators.note: was suggests the word once carried an extra part that it no longer has

parts.note: England under Oliver Cromwell was the Commonwealth (1649-60)
taken as written

explanation.surface: Under Cromwell luxury was ordinary — a history-book claim about Puritan England.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads cryptically as 'this word was prefixed by common under Cromwell': strip COMMON from COMMONWEALTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth means riches, the condition of living in luxury and plenty.

clue.text: Hard on grandpa as daughter's taken armrest

indicators.note: on means placed above in a down clue

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: taken means removed from the word for grandpa

parts.note: an oldster is an elderly person
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Grandpa is hard on his daughter who has taken his armrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' removes D from OLDSTER; 'as' is a link. 'armrest' reads as a chair part but means a rest for a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a case where a gun, or arm, is kept, so it is a rest for arms.

clue.text: Finished with wife in pub conflict

indicators.note: in places these letters within the word for the pub

parts.note: a bar is another word for a pub
o'er is a poetic contraction of over, meaning finished

explanation.surface: A man has finished with his wife and there is a fight in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: O'ER is the poetic contraction of over; 'with' is a link. The Boer War was fought in South Africa between Britain and the Boer republics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boer War was an armed conflict between Britain and the Boers in South Africa.

clue.text: Bookmaker who prepares the tea?

definitions.meaning: ... Dictionary of Phrase and Fable was compiled by Ebenezer ...
someone who brews makes the tea

explanation.surface: A betting man who also makes the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a turf accountant, but it is the compiler of a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Brewer produced a famous reference book, and anyone brewing tea prepares it.

clue.text: As reflex investigator cut off a bit of meringue

indicators.note: cut off means the named letter is removed from the end

parts.note: a pavlova is a meringue dessert

explanation.surface: A scientist studying reflexes cuts off a piece of meringue dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Pavlov studied conditioned reflexes in dogs.

clue.text: What's first needed for injury?

parts.note: read as a riddle: what follows the word 'first' to name the treatment needed for an injury

explanation.surface: A first-aid quiz question about what an injury needs first.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid means help, and first aid is the immediate help given to an injured person.

clue.text: Sluggish transport? On the contrary

parts.note: a slug is a bullet, so 'slug-ish' transport is named after one, yet it is very fast, not slow

explanation.surface: A complaint about slow trains, immediately contradicted.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese high-speed train is nicknamed after a gun's projectile, also called a slug.

clue.text: Assistant caught second remark, incidentally

indicators.note: caught means the assistant holds the letter inside

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: An assistant is caught making a second offhand comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' puts S inside AIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark made in passing, an incidental comment.

clue.text: Piece of Debussy that's not so powerful

definitions.meaning: ... is Debussy's orchestral work about the sea

explanation.surface: A critic finds a Debussy work rather feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Debussy wrote La Mer, and 'lamer' is the comparative of lame, meaning weaker.

clue.text: Having exercise machine, fight against bit of spare tyre

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the fight goes beside the tyre part

parts.note: the tread is part of a tyre
a mill is old slang for a fist fight

explanation.surface: Someone with a spare tyre of belly fat fights it on a gym machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare tyre' suggests a paunch, but it is a literal tyre. MILL is old boxing slang for a fight; 'Having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a gym machine with a moving belt for walking or running.

clue.text: Parliament misses Liberal — Lloyd George?

indicators.note: misses means the letter is left out

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: Parliament misses a Liberal prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: David Lloyd George was Welsh, and Dai is the Welsh pet form of David, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Dai is a Welsh form of David, the first name of the Welsh statesman.

clue.text: Any Verdi production may have intoxicating results

indicators.note: a production of these words makes something new from their letters

explanation.surface: Seeing any Verdi opera staged may leave you drunk with pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' suggests an opera staging, but it signals rearranging ANY VERDI.
explanation.definitionFit: A vineyard produces grapes for wine, so its results can be intoxicating.

clue.text: Piece of engine favoured by Lilliputian rebels

definitions.meaning: the larger end of a connecting rod, at the crankshaft
in Gulliver's Travels, rebels insisted on breaking eggs at the larger end

explanation.surface: An engine part linked to the rebels of Swift's Lilliput.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an engine component and the egg end preferred by Swift's satirical rebels.
